description: Engine evals for the deck pipeline. These are deliberately PACK-FREE: they exercise narrative, design briefs and orchestration, and none of them assert a colour, a token name or a footer string. Anything that can only be judged against a particular brand — seeded brand-audit violations, the off-brand regression fixture — lives with the PACK that defines what off-brand means, under <pack>/evals/. That is the same engine/brand line the rest of the repository is built on: the pack owns the fixtures that prove the pack can defend itself, and it travels with them.

evals.name: designer-two-column-sparse
evals.prompt: You are deck-designer inside the pipeline. The deck folder contains evals/stage-designer/deck-brief.md (copy it in). Execute the visual concept brief in evals/stage-designer/brief-01-two-column.md: generate the single slide as 08-risks.html plus your generation report.
evals.expected_output: One self-contained slide HTML (03-two-column family) + generation report
assertions: qa.py (validate + check_contrast + check_overflow) exits 0 on the produced slide
Generation report names the exact template file read (03-two-column.html or a variant)
Paired risk/mitigation rows use ONE shared CSS grid with explicit grid-row per pair (not two independent column stacks)
Density: atomic-item count ≤ 8 (sparse) and the report states count vs budget
Generation report names one focal point
Slide title is a complete assertion, not a label

evals.name: designer-data-chart-dense
evals.prompt: You are deck-designer inside the pipeline. The deck folder contains evals/stage-designer/deck-brief.md (copy it in; this eval overrides Density to dense). Execute evals/stage-designer/brief-02-chart.md: generate the single slide as 06-ingestion.html plus your generation report.
evals.expected_output: One slide with an ECharts bar chart (SVG renderer) + KPI panel + generation report
assertions: qa.py exits 0 on the produced slide
ECharts config copied from charts/ reference (renderer: 'svg' present; only data arrays and labels changed)
Chart title states the INSIGHT (sub-linear cost), not the topic ('Monthly ingestion')
KPI side panel present (bg-ds-light-blue family cards)
Density: 12 bars + 3 KPI cards ≤ 14 (dense) and the report states count vs budget

evals.name: designer-bespoke-rings-delegation
evals.prompt: You are deck-designer inside the pipeline. The deck folder contains evals/stage-designer/deck-brief.md (copy it in). Execute evals/stage-designer/brief-03-bespoke-svg.md: generate the single slide as 04-governance.html plus your generation report.
evals.expected_output: One slide whose right two-thirds is a bespoke concentric-rings SVG
assertions: The ring geometry is delegated to svg-reconstruct (donut/hub-spoke family recipe), NOT hand-authored arc path strings — the report says so
qa.py exits 0 on the produced slide
The bespoke SVG is the focal point; no competing card grid beside it
SVG follows design-system rules: defs starter-kit ids, primary labels ≥20px bold, sub-labels ≥16px
Density: ≤ 8 atomic items (labeled SVG nodes count) and the report states count vs budget
WebKit render (deck-review/scripts/render.py) shows no missing strokes (known-issues §5)

evals.name: designer-big-stat-breather
evals.prompt: You are deck-designer inside the pipeline. The deck folder contains evals/stage-designer/deck-brief.md (copy it in). Execute evals/stage-designer/brief-04-breather.md: generate the single slide as 07-roi.html plus your generation report.
evals.expected_output: One big-stat breather slide (36-big-stat family): hero numeral + assertion + support strip
assertions: qa.py exits 0 on the produced slide
Template read is 36-big-stat.html (report names it)
Hero numeral uses the display scale (≥120px, weight 300 or the ds-stat token role)
Density: 4 atomic items — nothing added beyond the brief
Gradient text, if used, covers ≤3 accent words

evals.name: narrative-briefs-complete
evals.prompt: You are deck-narrative inside the pipeline. Input: evals/stage-narrative/skeleton.json (locked brief + approved 9-slide skeleton; deck-brief at evals/stage-designer/deck-brief.md). Produce the narrative outline and one visual concept brief per skeleton slide in the SLIDE BRIEF format.
evals.expected_output: 9 complete SLIDE BRIEFs + outline with flow notes
assertions: Exactly 9 briefs, one per skeleton slide, in order
Every brief has ALL fields: Message, Structure, Visual, Key data, Emphasis, Audience, Density
Visual-rhythm floor met: ≥3 briefs with Visual ≠ none, including ≥1 bespoke (variance high, 9 slides)
No two adjacent briefs resolve to the same layout shape
Every Density line is sized to the sparse budget (≤8 items)
Every Message is a complete assertion (no label titles)
In-pipeline mode respected: no questions addressed directly to the user

evals.name: pptx-export-fidelity
evals.prompt: Run pptx-export on an assembled deck that contains at least: one gradient-background cover, one slide with a bespoke SVG diagram, one slide with gradient-accent title words, and one mixed-size card list. Then run the verification checklist from pptx-export/SKILL.md.
assertions: ir_preview.py exits 0: every slide content-MAE < 60 (blurred, ink-masked metric)
Text pt sizes in the pptx equal IR px * 0.5 exactly (spot-check one title run)
Mixed containers keep their direct text (no vanished table columns): every IR text total matches the page's innerText coverage
Zero raster nodes for gradient-text elements (grep IR: no raster node whose source element used background-clip:text)
Diagram SVGs are native grouped shapes: grpSp count == convertible-SVG count, custGeom freeforms present, zero .svg parts left unless a fallback printed its reason
svg2shapes.py --verify passes (content-MAE < 60) on every converted SVG asset
Gradient-background slides carry native gradFill (slide XML) with editable text shapes, not a full-slide picture
Every text run uses a per-weight font name (no bare 'System Sans' + bold flag)
All textboxes have wrap='none' and explicit paragraphs matching the browser's line breaks
With --native-charts: ECharts slides contain a real chart shape whose series data matches the page's chart.getOption()

evals.name: pharma-data-pitch
evals.description: Executive pitch deck for pharma data modernization (Snowflake migration)
evals.prompt: I need to pitch a data modernization engagement to PharmaCore Inc., a large pharma company currently using legacy SAP BW. We're proposing a migration to Snowflake + Databricks for real-time analytics. Audience is mostly executives (C-suite + steering committee). We want a 10-slide pitch that covers: current pain, proposed vision, architecture, risk mitigation, investment, timeline, and call-to-action. Make it strong — this is a €2M engagement.
evals.expected_output: A complete on-brand deck (HTML slides + index.html + PDF) with 10 slides covering the pitch narrative. All slides pass brand compliance and design quality audits; review gate cleared before PDF.
acceptance_criteria: Brand audit passes on all slides (no contrast violations, tokens used correctly)
Design crit approves all slides AND the deck-level pass (variance dial, no template monotony)
Review gate: zero open annotations + explicit acceptance before pdf-export
PDF exports cleanly (element screenshots; page count == slide_count)
Deck tells cohesive story (Pyramid Principle: conclusion first, then support)

evals.name: quarterly-status-update
evals.description: Quarterly status update for internal the brand data platform team
evals.prompt: We need a quarterly status update for Q2 2026 on our internal data platform modernization project. Audience is mixed: data engineers, platform architects, and a few business stakeholders. Target 7 slides. Must include: status summary (on track), what was delivered this quarter (3 key features), what's in progress, risks (one major: data governance complexity), and next quarter roadmap. Tone should be professional but informal — this is internal.
evals.expected_output: A compact 7-slide internal deck; fast-track intake acceptable (internal, low variance); all audits pass; PDF ready to email.
acceptance_criteria: Status updates are assertive (not labels): 'Q2 delivery on track: 87% sprint completion' not just 'Status Update'
Charts/metrics use insight titles ('Data ingestion grew 3x' not 'Monthly Ingestion Rates')
PDF exports and is readable on screen and in print

evals.name: capability-brief
evals.description: Capability brief for the brand's new AI/ML platform offering
evals.prompt: the brand is launching a new AI/ML platform service. We need a capability brief to market this to clients in pharma and manufacturing. Executive audience. 8 slides. Must position our 3 core capabilities: model development, MLOps automation, and business intelligence integration. Include competitive positioning, methodology, customer success stories (2), and call-to-action for a discovery call. This is a presales deck — make it compelling.
evals.expected_output: An 8-slide capability brief; all slides assertive and principle-driven; passes all audits and the review gate.
acceptance_criteria: Capability positioning is clear (understand what the brand does in AI/ML, why it's different)
Success stories include metrics (% efficiency gain, timeline to value, cost savings)
Design hierarchy supports presales narrative (confidence-building, not overwhelming)
Brand compliance and design quality both pass; review gate cleared
PDF is polished and ready for client distribution

test_instructions.stage_evals: Run each stage eval in an isolated working folder (copy the listed files in). Grade with scripts where possible: qa.py for designer outputs, seeded-violations.json recall/precision for the audit eval, field-presence checks for narrative briefs. These are the evals to iterate on after any change to a sub-skill.
test_instructions.acceptance_evals: Invoke the orchestrator with the prompt as the user request and walk the full 10-phase pipeline (intake → structure → narrative → design → audits incl. deck-level crit → assembly → render → review gate → pdf-export). Run before declaring a pipeline-wide change done — not for every iteration.
test_instructions.success_definition: Stage tier: all scripted assertions pass. Acceptance tier: all acceptance criteria met, designer never self-judges, review gate enforced.

pack_evals.note: Run these against whichever pack is active. A pack ships its own fixtures because the expected violations depend on its palette, type scale and footer.
pack_evals.harness: forge/scripts/verify_pack.py --pack <pack>  (templates must pass, off-brand-fixture must fail)
